gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the 16-inch 16:10 2560x1600 panel at 120 Hz or more (the MacBook Pro 16 match) sells for $189.99 to $247.99 from three models today (UPERFECT GR16DQ, UPERFECT GR16EQ, Mobile Pixels Duex Float 2 Pro), against $509.58 for the SOTSU FlipAction Pro 16 Gen 2, the only such screen ChatGPT showed.
standout_why: Compared against Macworld (updated 2026-11-25), PCWorld (updated 2026-06-26), TechRadar (updated 2026-11-20) and RTINGS. Macworld has part of it: it lists the Duex Float 2 Pro as 2560x1600 at 120 Hz at $299.99 when reviewed, but names no other 16-inch 16:10 120 Hz screen, does not mention ProMotion or 16:10, and its only UPERFECT entries are the stacked Delta Max and Delta Mega. PCWorld's only 2560x1600 screen is the 14.3-inch 75 Hz HP 514pn. Caveat: the RTINGS fetch returned navigation only (its three picks were not readable) and the TechRadar fetch was truncated to the MSI Pro MP165 E6 plus an Arzopa Z3FC caption, so those two are not fully checked. The Yahoo, PCMag and rottenwifi results were not opened.
decides: On the page's line (16-inch, 16:10, 2560x1600, 120 Hz or more as each maker states), the UPERFECT GR16EQ leads on the two ranking figures the stores state: 144 Hz and 450 cd/m2 at $199.99. That is $48.00 less than the Duex Float 2 Pro (120 Hz, 350 nits per Macworld, 2.9 lb) and $309.59 less than the SOTSU FlipAction Pro 16 Gen 2 (120 Hz, 400 nits). Every ChatGPT top pick misses the line: espresso Pro 15 and ViewSonic VX1655-4K-OLED are 3840x2160 (16:9), and the Arzopa Z3FC is 2560x1440 (16:9). This confirms the desk order: GR16EQ is the pick, the Float 2 Pro takes the stacked-above-the-MacBook segment, and the Fold 16 QHD is a row only (220 nits, no refresh rate stated). The page should print both GR16EQ weights (0.75 kg in the copy, 1.04 kg in the spec table). An Amazon listing titled 'UPERFECT 2.5K 240Hz 16" 2560x1600' at $208.97 may outrank the GR16EQ on refresh; its brightness and weight were not read, so check it before publishing.
